name: Our Lady of Sorrows Basilica
architect: Henry Engelbert, John F. Pope and William J. Brinkmann
history: Founded in 1874 and run by the Servite friars ever since, the parish broke ground for its church on 17 June 1890 and dedicated it on 5 January 1902. Its Sorrowful Mother Novena drew worshippers from across the country and many more by radio. The church was named a basilica in 1956. It once had twin towers; the west tower was lost to a fire in 1984.
arch: A restrained Renaissance Revival front of rusticated stone with round-arched windows, and a surviving 200-foot east tower; inside, a coffered barrel vault 80 feet high and 65 feet wide wraps around a Carrara marble altar.
features: It houses the National Shrine of St. Peregrine, patron of people with cancer.
The nave has more than 1,100 gold-leaf panels.

look.d: The survivor of twin towers rises 200 feet, masonry halfway, then timber, sheet metal and tile.
The plain front hides one of Chicago's richest interiors.

fun: A scene of The Untouchables (1987) was filmed here, with Sean Connery and Kevin Costner.
journal: Plain stone outside, a golden barrel vault inside. One tower left standing.

quiz.q: Which order has run the parish since 1874?
What happened to the west tower in 1984?
